item.description:
Changes since v0.2.24:
- A triage script reads the anonymous daily summaries from PostHog and files one GitHub issue per firing rule (#143) - Every merge that changes app logic is released at once by the agent that merged it (#142) - Ensemble sends one anonymous usage summary a day to PostHog, on by default with one switch to turn it off (#141) - A still head no longer lets one isolated camera reading carry the resting dot away (#140) - Nose dot is off on a new install, and the first-run tour asks whether to show it (#136)

Changes since v0.2.23:
- Facing an archived session outlines its Unarchive bar instead of drawing no outline (#133)

Changes since v0.2.22:
- Ensemble restarts itself once when Accessibility is granted, so the grant takes effect with no button press - The repository has a 1280 by 640 social preview image of the hero, with the command that regenerates it - Checks compile the release binary once and run the replay-timeline tests; the contributor guide lists every script and the real release route - Home page gets a gallery of eight looping vignettes: incredibly intuitive (#132) - Menu bar icon shows an upgrade arrow while a newer version is found (#131) - Website browser test takes the Chrome path from an environment variable and starts as root on Linux (#130) - Demo page shows only an 'available on desktop' message on phones and tablets (#129) - Demo menu panel: the camera row is a picker like the app's (#128) - Add the website review runbook and a "Demo available on desktop" button on phones (#127) - Website: desktop-first demo, friends section, clean letter and how-it-works (#126) - Update schedule text names the General settings and the hourly check; release notes cover both updaters on one Mac (#125) - Release notes list pull requests merged by squash as well as by merge commit (#124) - The peace sign widens the session to the chat's default width, so other sessions give up only the space that needs (#123) - While you pinch and drag to scroll, the nose dot shows the scroll arrows (#122) - Website animations are straight and larger, with a caption on each saying what to notice (#121) - Automatic camera starts a calibrated camera first; a missing permission shows one button (#120) - Choose the camera from the menu bar panel (#119) - With the lid closed, each dictation first moves the Mac's input to a microphone that works (#118) - Dictation safety records cannot be redirected by a planted link, and a deleted record stays deleted after a crash (#117) - Shipping a release warns before the local signing certificate expires and refuses after it (#115) - Update (#114) - Shorten the README's Security and limits section to one-line promises and a defaults paragraph (#113) - README install is two sentences; setup and calibration detail moves to a docs page (#112) - Add dependency review, CodeQL and Scorecard workflows (#111) - Each release's update feed entry carries the same notes as its release page (#110) - The rule that keeps the dictation safety record while a start press is in flight is decided in one tested place (#109)
